country: International (Germany-based task analysis across 6 ICUs; international Delphi survey)
sample_unit: Delphi participants (19 data scientists, 61 ICU clinicians: 25 physicians and 36 nurses)
unlisted_practices: Selecting task-specific levels of human-AI teaming (augmentation vs automation) for ICU tasks using Delphi consensus of data scientists and clinicians
Excluding AI from patient interaction tasks due to ethical concerns and importance of the clinician-patient relationship
Shifting to full automation (level 4) or reducing to no AI (level 1) when interpretability, predictability, and control conditions are not met
Prioritizing interpretability, predictability, and control in regulation when clinicians hold full accountability

screen.reason: Multimethod empirical study combining task analysis across 6 ICUs and a Delphi survey of clinicians and data scientists to assess optimal levels of human-AI teaming/automation across ICU tasks.
